description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/ref.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  5 blessed rows.

perl marks a LITERAL's SV read-only, so anything aliased to one refuses a
write.  PROBED (scratch/s473t6a/probes/misc1.pl D1/D2, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL
2ac855aa):

    eval { for (1) { $_ = 2 } }          perl DIES "Modification of a
    eval { my $r = \(1); $$r = 2 }        read-only value attempted"
                                          PCL  LIVES, both

Rows in t/op/ref.t (tests 230, 232-235), now carrying this task:
  * `assignment to value aliased to literal number`   / `â¦ literal string`
  * `refgen does not allow assignment to value aliased to literal number`
    / `â¦ literal string`
  * `weaken refuses to weaken a read-only ref`

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: a read-only bit on the p-box, set by the literal
constructor and by the foreach aliasing of a literal list, and consulted by
`box-set` / `p-scalar-=` / the element write paths.  That is a WRITE-PATH
change on the hottest sites in the runtime, which is why this is filed rather
than fixed in a triage round: measure the cost of one flag test in `box-set`
before designing (the s485 rule -- a new arm on a hot path is MEASURED on the
path it sits on).

RELATED, already documented: `docs/not-supported.md` "Read-only constants via
\undef stash tricks" names the same absence for a different spelling, and
`perl-tests/ref.t`'s registry rows sit on it.  A fix should close both.
subject: A value ALIASED TO A LITERAL is read-only in perl and writable in PCL: for (1) { $_ = 2 } and \(1) both live -- 5 rows in t/op/ref.t
